data_fields.name: hitch rule (drop backlog past the cap)
fixed step (from the server tick rate)

best_idea: Drive every fixed step from one frame accumulator with a per-frame cap, draw the gap between the last two steps with a clamped alpha, and decay corrections by 1 - exp(-dt/smoothMs) so a server correction eases out instead of snapping.
decision_why: The accumulator, clamped alpha and frame-rate-independent decay fit a fast phone fight; adapt the hitch rule so a long hitch carries its backlog instead of dropping inputs, and make the cap a data field. Predicting enemies is rejected because enemy state comes from the server.
acceptance: On a phone with a 120 Hz display and a 30 Hz fight step, the hero and attackers move without stutter; after a server correction the hero eases to the corrected pose over about one patch interval instead of snapping; a test asserts that a 200 ms hitch (six steps at 30 Hz, over the cap of five) sends every queued input in order with none dropped.
